newsitem.title: USA: DC control board calls White House plan "historic".
newsitem.headline: DC control board calls White House plan "historic".

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board on Tuesday called the President's new federal aid proposal for the city "bold and constructive."
The White House this morning announced a $3.9 billion, five-year aid package for the financially struggling city.

"Based on our review of the plan so far, it is clear that the President proposed an historic allignment of the Federal-District relationship," Andrew Brimmer, chairman of the five-member panel, said in a press statement.
"It represents the first time that the Federal Government has agreed to view the District as a city and not as a state," Brimmer said.
"A change of this magnitude can make an enormous, positive contribution to the improvement of public services in the District of Columbia," he said.
Brimmer said the board is doing a detailed examination of the plan, which he said includes some "serious tradeoffs."
For example, the present $660 million annual payment Congress makes to the city would be eliminated, Brimmer said.
"At the same time, by assuming the responsibility to fund a number of State-like functions and programs, the Federal government would provide the City with some amount of budgetary relief," he said.
